title: You cant backtest gamma walls, because nobody sells the old open interest by strike to rebuild them
author: person-person12
selftext:
I wanted to test a setup built on dealer gamma walls going back a decade, and I spent a week finding out the data to do it is not for sale anywhere.

A call wall or a gamma flip is a computed level. What it gets computed from is the open interest at every strike on that day, plus where price was sitting. Almost nobody keeps that. Exchanges and vendors hand you todays chain and then overwrite it, so last Tuesdays strike by strike open interest is gone unless somebody was writing it down last Tuesday. One of the chain sources we were reading retired its historical chains outright last month, which took another few years of it off the table.

So the levels in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) start the day we started recording them, 7 May this year, and a build that reads them gets tested from 8 May and says so on the result. There is a published daily net gamma figure for the S&P going back to 2011 that is real history, and it is a different calculation to a wall on a futures contract, so we dont staple the two together to make the chart look longer than it is.

Its the school report card thing. You can get this terms grades, and you can get the final average for every year back to 2011, and no amount of asking gets you the mark on one specific test in 2014, because the paper went in the bin that June.

Which means any gamma backtest carrying ten years of history was computed from something other than the open interest of those ten years of days.
